stories.title: Global Holdings Lands $382M Refi for Midtown Tower
stories.excerpt: Private equity firm Global Holdings has secured a $382.4 million refinancing loan for its Midtown Manhattan office tower at 120 Park Ave., with Wells Fargo and German bank LBBW originating the note. The funding, reported by The Real Deal, retires the property’s existing $335 million loan from HSBC. The recapitalization follows Bloomberg LP’s renewal in late 2025 of its 495,753-square-foot lease across 20 floors of the Class A building, marking one of the city’s largest lease deals of the year. Bloomberg’s lease, which was extended to 2024, accounts for roughly 80% of the property’s rentable area. Global Holdings acquired the 620,000-square-foot building neighboring Grand Central Terminal from Altria Group in 2008. The refinancing will facilitate a capital improvement program for the asset, which was built in 1981. Chaired by Eyal Ofer, Global Holdings has an international real estate portfolio spanning more than 10 million square feet of real estate, including 120 properties and over 1,500 hotel rooms. The post Global Holdings Lands $382M Refi for Midtown Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Global Holdings refinanced 120 Park Ave. Manhattan for $382.4M at Wells Fargo, LBBW.
Bloomberg renewed 495,753-sf lease through 2024, anchoring ~80% of building.
Refi funds capital improvements on 1981 Class A office tower near Grand Central.
stories.summary: Global Holdings secured a $382.4M refinance from Wells Fargo and LBBW for its Midtown Manhattan office tower at 120 Park Ave., replacing a $335M HSBC loan. Bloomberg's renewal of its 495,753-sf lease (80% of building) and extension to 2024 drove the recapitalization. Capital improvement proceeds support asset modernization for the 620,000-sf Class A building built in 1981 near Grand Central Terminal.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Office tower refinance in Manhattan signals lender willingness to extend debt on stabilized, blue-chip-tenant-anchored office, but tells us little about residential demand or supply in NYC markets. No chain of effect to apartment fundamentals.

stories.title: NYC Plans 215-Unit Bronx Apartment Building
stories.excerpt: New York City’s Department of Housing Preservation & Development (HPD) has filed plans for a 215-unit apartment building on a vacant city-owned lot in the Bronx’s Melrose neighborhood. The 176,000-square-foot building at 3116–3124 Third Ave. would rise 20 stories, the New York Business Journal reported, citing plans filed with the New York City Planning Commission. HPD revealed that it has chosen Bronx-based developer Procida Cos. and community development nonprofit Nos Quedamos for the project. The building would also come with 7,000 square feet of commercial space and amenities including a community room, second-floor terrace and roof terrace. If realized, the project would advance the Melrose Commons Urban Renewal Plan, which proposes to bring new affordable housing across a 33-block area. To make way for the project, HPD is requesting that the city remove the 85-foot height limit for new multifamily developments in the vicinity. The department has also asked the Planning Commission create an Urban Development Action Area Program within the neighborhood that would set forth guidelines for developing income-restricted and affordable housing. The post NYC Plans 215-Unit Bronx Apartment Building appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NYC HPD planning 215-unit apartment building in Bronx Melrose neighborhood.
Procida Cos. + Nos Quedamos selected; includes 100–120 affordable units.
HPD seeking height-limit waiver from 85 feet, creation of UDAAP designation.
stories.summary: NYC's Department of Housing Preservation & Development filed plans for a 215-unit, 20-story apartment building on city-owned land at 3116–3124 Third Ave. in Melrose, Bronx. Developers Procida Cos. and Nos Quedamos will deliver 100–120 affordable units alongside 7,000 sf of retail and community amenities. HPD is requesting a height-limit waiver and Urban Development Action Area Program designation to fast-track affordable housing delivery across the 33-block Melrose Commons renewal area.
stories.impact: Signals strong public-sector commitment to Melrose affordable housing pipeline and zoning flexibility. The UDAAP and height-limit waiver removal lower regulatory friction for future private development in the submarket, improving feasibility. Expect accelerated competition and density gains in South Bronx; monitor whether City incentives (PILOT, TIF) expand to attract private multifamily investment alongside HPD's institutional supply.

stories.title: Northern New Jersey Shopping Center Changes Hands
stories.excerpt: Adoni Property Group has acquired the 60,614-square-foot shopping center in Northern New Jersey’s Basking Ridge from Kushner Real Estate Group. JLL Capital Markets arranged the sale and secured $12.2 million in acquisition financing on behalf of the buyer through an unidentified life insurance firm. Built in 2000, the community retail center spans approximately 11 acres at 546 Allen Rd. and includes five buildings that were fully leased to 18 tenants at the time of the sale. Four new leases executed within the past 12 months point to continued momentum at the property. Anchored by Walgreens and United States Postal Service locations, the shopping center sits within the master-planned community The Hills at Basking Ridge. “Highlands Village is a premier, necessity-based retail center with a proven history of stability and long-term tenant loyalty,” said Sonny Adoni, founder and CEO of Adoni Property Group in a statement. Westfield, NJ-based Adoni develops and manages a diversified portfolio of residential and commercial properties. Headquartered in Jersey City, Kushner Real Estate Group is a real estate investment and management firm with a portfolio of apartments and commercial space across four states. The post Northern New Jersey Shopping Center Changes Hands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Adoni Property Group acquired 60,614-sf shopping center in Basking Ridge, NJ for undisclosed price.
JLL arranged $12.2M acquisition financing; center fully leased to 18 tenants.
Retail asset, not multifamily; minimal relevance to apartment development.
stories.summary: Adoni Property Group bought a fully-leased, 60,614-sf shopping center in Basking Ridge, Northern New Jersey from Kushner Real Estate Group, with JLL securing $12.2M in acquisition financing from a life insurance firm. The 11-acre property built in 2000 is anchored by Walgreens and USPS, with four new leases signed in the past 12 months.
stories.impact: No material impact to multifamily development. Retail asset sale does not signal employment, population, or housing demand shifts in Northern New Jersey.

stories.title: Iconic Rancho Cordova Furniture Showroom Listed for Sale
stories.excerpt: The longtime Rancho Cordova showroom of Beck’s Furniture has been listed for sale. The 208,800-square-foot property at 11840 Folsom Blvd has served primarily as a warehouse and distribution center for Beck’s Furniture, where people came to view the chairs and sofas before buying. The company closed its doors last year. The 10 acres along the Highway 50 corridor and has served as one of Northern California’s most recognizable furniture destinations for nearly 50 years. It features an approximately 90,000 square feet of showroom space and 120,000 square feet of warehouse and distribution space. Morrow Botros, Bryce MacDonald and Jay Hamer of Cushman & Wakefield have been exclusively retained to market the asset on behalf of the seller, Beck’s Furniture & Sleep / Beckinger Family Ownership.  Botros added, “For nearly 50 years, the Beck’s Furniture campus has stood as one of the Sacramento region’s most recognizable commercial landmarks. Few properties can claim both institutional scale and deep community recognition.” The post Iconic Rancho Cordova Furniture Showroom Listed for Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Beck's Furniture's 208,800-sf Rancho Cordova showroom listed for sale after company closure.
10-acre Highway 50 corridor property; 50-year institutional landmark in Sacramento region.
Cushman & Wakefield marketing; conversion or redevelopment potential unclear.
stories.summary: The Beck's Furniture showroom and warehouse at 11840 Folsom Blvd. in Rancho Cordova, California—a 208,800-sf, 10-acre landmark property along Highway 50—has been listed for sale following the company's closure last year. The asset includes ~90,000 sf of showroom and 120,000 sf of warehouse/distribution space. Cushman & Wakefield is exclusively marketing the property.
stories.impact: Potential land/redevelopment opportunity in Sacramento metro, but no demand signal is evident. Industrial/retail closure and sale alone do not indicate population inflow, employment growth, or rental demand. Monitor only if asset is rezoned or acquired for multifamily conversion; otherwise, supply-side relevance is dormant.

stories.title: Tishman Speyer Trades Mountain View Office Building for $121.5M
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer sold 400 Castro Street, a 100 percent leased, Class A office building in downtown Mountain View, California. Spear Street Capital was the buyer in the $121.5 million transaction. Tishman Speyer developed the 138,000-square-foot property in 2002 and immediately leased the office space in full to Fenwick & West, which has remained a customer in the building. Tishman Speyer claims the transaction represents one of the strongest pricing outcomes for a Mountain View office sale in recent years. Centrally located with convenient access to highways and Caltrain, 400 Castro features expansive roof decks, underground parking and views of the San Francisco Bay and coastal mountains. The property, which was 100% leased at the time of the sale, is located in the heart of Downtown Mountain View, surrounded by restaurants and retail, with Cascal restaurant, Peet’s Coffee, and Sweetgreen on site. Tishman Speyer was represented by the Eastdil Secured team led by Nate Jones. The post Tishman Speyer Trades Mountain View Office Building for $121.5M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tishman Speyer sold 400 Castro Street, Mountain View, CA for $121.5M to Spear Street Capital.
100% leased Class A office, 138,000 sf, tenant Fenwick & West since 2002.
Strong pricing outcome; reflects Mountain View office market tightness.
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer exited 400 Castro Street, a 138,000-sf, fully-leased Class A office building in downtown Mountain View, California, for $121.5M to Spear Street Capital. Fenwick & West has occupied the entire building since its 2002 completion. Tishman Speyer characterized the sale as among the strongest office pricing outcomes in Mountain View in recent years.
stories.impact: Office market strength and institutional investor demand in Mountain View does not translate to multifamily signals. No employment growth, corporate relocation, or population inflow drivers are indicated. Mountain View office fundamentals remain separate from residential rental markets; monitor only if office vacancy spikes or major tech layoffs suggest contrarian labor/demand shifts.

stories.title: Related Secures $65M Refi for Office Property in L.A.’s South Bay
stories.excerpt: The owners of a 301,000-square-foot Class A office property in Los Angeles’ South Bay have secured refinancing for the property. Owners Related Companies and Cruzan landed the $64.7 million loan from Waterfall Asset Management and Delaware Life for the eight-story property called the Torrance, named after its home city. The asset at 21250 Hawthorne Boulevard is 93 percent occupied, according to Yardi Matrix, with tenants including All Nippon Airways, Salon Republic, Barrister Executive Suites, Compass California, Unio Health Partners and Morgan Stanley. Newmark’s Jordan Roeschlaub, Nick Scribani and Chris Lozinak arranged the debt. The property was built in 1988. Related and Cruzan acquired it from Stream Realty Partners for $106.8 million in 2017, and secured $59.2 million in refinancing in 2022. The South Bay has benefited from surging demand from aerospace and defense users for both office and industrial space. But the Greater Los Angeles office market remains deeply bifurcated. Overall vacancy was at 25.3 percent after the second quarter, nearly unchanged from year-end 2025, while trophy properties have a 13.5 percent vacancy rate, according to Newmark research. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Related Companies and Cruzan refinanced South Bay L.A. office tower for $64.7M.
301,000-sf Class A property at 93% occupancy; aerospace/defense tenant mix.
South Bay benefits from aerospace, defense demand; broader LA office market bifurcated.
stories.summary: Related Companies and Cruzan secured a $64.7M refinance from Waterfall Asset Management and Delaware Life for the Torrance, a 301,000-sf, eight-story Class A office property in LA's South Bay at 21250 Hawthorne Boulevard. The property is 93% leased to tenants including All Nippon Airways, Morgan Stanley, and Unio Health Partners. The owners acquired the 1988-built asset from Stream Realty Partners for $106.8M in 2017.
stories.impact: South Bay aerospace-and-defense sector strength supports office demand and indicates job concentration that may drive multifamily rent growth in adjacent submarkets (Torrance, Manhattan Beach, Redondo Beach). However, broad LA office bifurcation and near-term oversupply in secondary markets limit spillover residential demand. Multifamily developers should monitor aerospace supply-chain expansion (SpaceX, Northrop Grumman, others) as a longer-term demand catalyst in South Bay submarkets.

stories.title: Ares Buys Two Fully Leased Miami Warehouses for $109M
stories.excerpt: Ares Management has acquired two fully leased warehouses in Miami-Dade County from BGRE for a combined $108.7 million, property records show. In the larger transaction, the L.A.-based asset manager paid $65.3 million for a 230,147-square-foot, 15-acre distribution center at 3811 West 108th Street, located between Florida Turnpike and Interstate 75 in Hialeah. National retailer Target is the distribution center’s sole tenant after signing a 10-year lease in 2022 with two five-year extension options, according to county records. In the second sale, Ares Management paid $43.4 million for a 142,472-square-foot, 8-acre warehouse about 13 miles south at 13190 Northwest 17th Street, west of the Florida Turnpike, near Sweetwater. E-commerce parcel delivery company LaserShip has leased the entire property. BGRE, formerly called Brookfield Properties, developed both buildings, completing them between 2022 and 2023. Since opening an office in Miami Beach in 2024, Ares Management has been making inroads in South Florida’s industrial market. Last year, it purchased a 230,976-square-foot warehouse in Weston for $56 million as well as a 456,219-square-foot industrial portfolio in Broward County for $121 million. A spokesperson for Ares declined to comment, while a representative for BGRE did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ares Management bought two Miami-Dade warehouses from BGRE for $108.7M total.
Target-leased 230,147-sf distribution center (Hialeah), LaserShip 142,472-sf (Sweetwater).
Both fully leased; industrial logistics strength in Miami corridor.
stories.summary: Ares Management acquired two fully-leased industrial warehouses in Miami-Dade County from BGRE (formerly Brookfield Properties) for a combined $108.7M. The larger asset—230,147 sf at 3811 West 108th Street in Hialeah—is leased to Target on a 10-year term (2022) with two five-year options. The second property—142,472 sf at 13190 Northwest 17th Street near Sweetwater—is leased to LaserShip. Both properties were developed by BGRE in 2022–2023.
stories.impact: Industrial strength and institutional capital flowing into Miami-Dade logistics does not directly signal multifamily demand. However, e-commerce and last-mile distribution hub expansion (Target, LaserShip anchor tenants) may drive job clustering and worker inflow, particularly in Hialeah and Sweetwater submarkets. Monitor wage growth, employment in logistics/distribution, and population migration into these trade-area neighborhoods; potential upstream residential demand 12–18 months out.

stories.title: Gaia Lands Another Extension for Williamsburg Apartments’ $48M Loan
stories.excerpt: It’s déjà vu for GAIA Real Estate. The developer landed for the second straight year a one-year extension for its $48 million loan on loan with Raymond James Bank backing a multifamily property at 55 Hope Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer can first report. The extension pushed the loan maturity to August 2027, which will be five years after Gaia acquired the 1907-built and 2012-renovated apartment building previously utilized as a pencil factory. “We acquired the property at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, amid significant uncertainty in New York, and have since increased net operating income significantly through active management and a long-term approach to value creation, Danny Fishman, CEO and co-founder at Gaia Real Estate, said in a statement. “This extension demonstrates our ability to identify opportunities across market cycles and position our investments for sustained performance in Brooklyn’s multifamily market.” Fishman added that lenders were interested in refinancing the loan given that the loan is less than 50 percent loan-to-value with a “very strong” debt service coverage ratio, but he opted to go the extension route due to the current rising interest rate climate. After purchasing the 117-unit property from Hope Street Capital for $80 million in August 2022, Gaia added coworking space and refurbished the building’s rooftop while also providing tenant concessions. Hope Street Capital acquired the building for $17 million in 2010 and converted it from industrial to residential use, The Real Deal previously reported. Raymond James Bank did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: GAIA Real Estate secured second consecutive one-year loan extension on Williamsburg apartment.
55 Hope Street, Brooklyn: $48M loan extended to August 2027.
Asset acquired during COVID-19 pandemic; NOI significantly increased through active management.
stories.summary: GAIA Real Estate obtained a second straight one-year extension on its $48M loan from Raymond James Bank for 55 Hope Street, a 1907-built, 2012-renovated apartment building in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. The extension pushed maturity to August 2027, five years after acquisition during the COVID-19 pandemic. CEO Danny Fishman highlighted significant NOI growth through active management, noting lender interest in refinancing reflects sustained performance.
stories.impact: Lender confidence in Brooklyn multifamily post-pandemic recovery and extended rate-lock availability signal resilient demand fundamentals and operational upside in Williamsburg. Loan extensions without forced sales or workouts indicate cap rates have stabilized and debt markets remain accessible for well-performing assets. Developers should view this as a green light to underwrite new multifamily starts in Brooklyn submarkets with similar lease-up and rent-growth trajectories; capital remains available for quality assets.

stories.title: Membership Platform Patreon Renews 45K-SF Sublease at 75 Varick Street
stories.excerpt: Patreon is staying put at its offices in Manhattan’s Hudson Square. The membership and monetization platform, which allows creators to build communities and share exclusive content, has signed a sublease renewal for 44,661 square feet at Hudson Square Properties’ 75 Varick Street, according to a monthly office report from CBRE. The renewal was confirmed by Patreon. It’s unclear when the San Francisco-based company moved into the 18-story office building, also known as One Hudson Square, or who the sublandlord is. 75 Varick is a flagship property within the Hudson Square Properties portfolio, which is owned through a joint venture involving Trinity Church Wall Street and Norges Bank Investment Management. Hines was also a minority investor and operating partner in the JV, but Commercial Observer reported in July that it would no longer hold its stake in the 13-property portfolio, and that Brookfield might replace Hines by securing a 10 percent stake in the portfolio. The length of Patreon’s renewal and the asking rent were unclear, but a report from Newmark found office rents in Hudson Square averaged $91.02 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026. The brokers involved in the deal were also unclear. Spokespeople for Hudson Square Properties and CBRE did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Patreon shares its 75 Varick building with several other tenants, including artificial intelligence productivity software developer Notion and creative production firm RadicalMedia, which both renewed leases there in January. In fact, renewal deals appear to be popular at 75 Varick, as media company Horizon Media signed a deal there in March 2025 to keep its 360,000 square feet for another 17 years. And it’s not just 75 Varick — the entire Hudson Square neighborhood has been reaping the benefits of the city’s AI boom and increased leasing demand. bullets: Patreon renewed 44,661-sf sublease at Hudson Square Properties' 75 Varick Street, Manhattan.
San Francisco tech company commitment to NYC office space.
Hudson Square portfolio owned by Trinity Church/Norges Bank; Hines exiting, Brookfield considering stake.
stories.summary: Patreon, a San Francisco-based membership and monetization platform, renewed its 44,661-sf sublease at Hudson Square Properties' 75 Varick Street (One Hudson Square) in Manhattan's Hudson Square neighborhood. The office property is part of a 13-property portfolio owned through a joint venture of Trinity Church Wall Street and Norges Bank Investment Management. Hines recently exited its stake, with Brookfield potentially acquiring a 10% stake.
stories.impact: Tech tenant renewals in Manhattan signal office fundamentals stabilization but do not drive multifamily demand directly. No employment growth, headcount expansion, or relocation signal is evident—merely lease renewal and space occupation. Monitor only if broader tech-sector NYC hiring accelerates; otherwise, office occupancy in Hudson Square has minimal spillover to residential rental fundamentals.

stories.title: Developer Ailanthus Files Plans to Build 400 Apartments at 424 Hoyt Street in Gowanus
stories.excerpt: Residential towers grow in Brooklyn. Affordable and mixed-income housing developer Ailanthus has filed a rezoning application with the New York City Department of City Planning to build a 17-story, 175-foot-tall mixed-use residential development at 424 Hoyt Street in Gowanus, Brooklyn. If approved, the building would have 400 apartment units — of which 100 to 120 would be affordable — as well as a 46,000-square-foot public school and 14,000 square feet of commercial retail space, according to the application filing. The application still has several steps to get through before approval is granted. “As noted in the Mamdani administration’s recently released report, New York City needs to create 700,000 new housing units over the next 10 years. While Gowanus contributed thousands of units in the last few years, Community Board 6, which encompasses Gowanus, was identified as one of three districts in Brooklyn with the least access to affordable homes, setting a target for thousands more units to be created there,” a spokesperson for Ailanthus told Commercial Observer. Two Trees Management acquired 424 Hoyt Street in July 2008 for $7.7 million, according to property records. Ailanthus, led by Ofer Cohen, Vivian Liao and Tucker Reed, has a ground lease at the site from Two Trees. Currently, there is a one-story automotive repair building and a vehicle storage facility on the property, which is allowed 91,800 buildable square feet. Two Trees Management declined Commercial Observer’s request for comment. Gowanus has been in the midst of a glow-up ever since its rezoning plan was initiated, not to mention a 2013 environmental cleanup plan designed to transform one of the city’s grittiest areas. The 82-block redevelopment plan passed in November of 2021. There have been several luxury and affordable housing developments delivered in Gowanus, including the Gowanus Wharf campus, 544 Carroll Street and 499 President Street. bullets: Ailanthus filed rezoning application for 400-unit, 17-story mixed-use at 424 Hoyt, Gowanus.
100–120 units affordable; includes 46,000-sf public school, 14,000-sf retail.
Community Board 6 identified as one of three Brooklyn districts with least affordable-housing access.
stories.summary: Affordable and mixed-income housing developer Ailanthus filed a rezoning application to build a 400-unit, 17-story mixed-use residential tower at 424 Hoyt Street in Gowanus, Brooklyn. The project includes 100–120 affordable units, a 46,000-sf public school, and 14,000 sf of commercial retail space. The filing references NYC's need to create 700,000 new housing units over 10 years and identifies Community Board 6 as one of three Brooklyn districts with the least access to affordable housing.
stories.impact: Gowanus continues to deliver high-density multifamily pipeline, supporting supply growth. However, City emphasis on affordable units and schooling reflects regulatory push toward income-restricted production that pressures both market-rate feasibility and returns. Ailanthus's project signals zoning flexibility in Gowanus, but financing and construction-cost headwinds (inflation, labor) remain material constraints. Developers should track whether mixed-income models (with density bonuses and public-school contributions) become the de facto standard in Brooklyn, reshaping pro-forma assumptions and capital sources.
